title: Hidden surface-elevation trace regularity for subcritical linearized two-dimensional irrotational shallow-water transmission systems with an interior elliptic region
source_title: A priori estimates for the moving contact line problem for the $2D$ nonlinear shallow water equations with a partially immersed obstacle
author: Tatsuo Iguchi; David Lannes
difficulty_reason: The usual trace theorem and the available weakly dissipative bulk-energy estimate do not control the selected boundary component at the required regularity. The authors build compensated characteristic fields for the variable-coefficient exterior system and cancel the mixed surface-elevation flux against the already-authored bulk-energy identity. Their new interior Rellich identities convert all remaining normal/tangential boundary products into controlled volume source terms, yielding the trace bound under only the printed time-integrable coefficient derivative assumptions.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Proposition4.1: regular solutions of exact linearized exterior system3.13, two transmission conditions3.14 and interior elliptic system3.15, under Assumption3.2(i)–(iv) on subcritical flow, positive bounded interior depth, positive diffeomorphism Jacobian/bounded spatial derivative, and L1-in-time L-infinity bounds on coefficient derivatives. The surface-elevation good-unknown trace has the stated L2-in-space-time estimate in terms of sup bulk energy and time-integrated source norms. The independent boundary evolution3.16 is not assumed by the chosen proposition (Remark4.2). Full authored characteristic fields31–32, cancellation of boundary integrals33–34, Rellich identities34–37 and closing estimate37 read. Exact definitions/fixed-domain transform18–23 and assumptions24 included. Toy-model explanation29–30 and full weak-dissipativity energy proof25–28 read, although4.1 itself does not need Proposition3.4 to estimate its RHS bulk energy. Standard smooth extension operators are explicitly used26/35 with norm bounds; no missing local new core. Later regularizing-diffeomorphism and second-order nonlinear good-unknown construction Sections5–7 remain unreviewed and the main nonlinear a priori theorem is not counted. Physical6 text extraction exposes redundant hidden draft text in an embedded figure resource; rendering the original page shows a clean publisher figure and equations, with no visible overlay/content defect. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors combine characteristic fields of a weakly dissipative hyperbolic boundary with Rellich identities for the interior elliptic velocity potential to recover a space-time trace estimate unavailable from the usual bulk energy or trace theorem. This coupled hyperbolic-elliptic free-boundary analysis exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
